epic.title: epic-418-followon — F, C, E
epic.intent_and_why: Finish epic #418: land the MCP front door (F, #424) and the first relocation tranche (C, #421), then re-cut what survives and check what shipped against what each workstream promised (E, #423).

definition_of_done: F: the six done-conditions in spec section F, with DC5 (spine-management cost, counted from the call record, both sides of the door) as the acceptance measure
C: an agent at gate N does not do, plan or reserve gate N+k work; per-run delivered tokens do not grow
E: every survivor of the redux appears in exactly one of the current wave or the forecast, and shipped-vs-obligation is checked across both sets of work

good_enough.mandatory_quality: A claim about what happened brings its evidence. A measured negative is a complete deliverable; an UNMEASURED condition is not a negative and is never reported as one.
good_enough.sufficient_evidence: One-shot live scripts kept runnable, not CI-wired; green + independently reviewed for merge
good_enough.appetite: Rigor scales with cost-to-undo, not uniformly

hard_constraints: The CLI door stays; F is additive
No engine logic duplicated — the server wraps the engine's own dispatch
The gate imperative rides tool results verbatim; spine templates stay the single source of instruction text
settings.json is never written at any scope
Cheap fixes are routed, not implemented inside a wave under measurement
fixed_decisions: Execution order F -> C -> E is a dependency order, not a schedule
E is terminal by its own body
C's tranche boundary and E's cluster boundaries are costly-to-revert and surfaced

current_wave.objective: Land F: the MCP front door, with its acceptance measured rather than asserted
exit_criteria: F's six done-conditions each carry a verdict backed by evidence
no gate left blocked by its own reviewer

issues.title: MCP front door for the engine — ~7 typed tools wrapping the dispatch loop
issues.desired_outcome: A second front door that moves spine-management cost off the working agent's attention, with the cost drop measured.
issues.useful_now: F settles the verb contract C must relocate against, and it is the epic's least-proven piece — finding out early is the point of the reorder.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: DC5 counted from the call record, both arms, both sides of the door, CLI baseline re-measured rather than reused
issues.implementation_latitude: Tool grouping, argument shapes, delivery mechanism, tracer protocol and n, what is lifted from the prototype
hard_constraints_no_gos: do not gold-plate the tool grouping
local_unknowns: whether an in-session Task-tool subagent shares its parent's already-launched MCP server

wave_forecast.outcome: C (#421): first relocation tranche against F's settled verb contract
wave_forecast.why_likely: F is the stated dependency and its verb surface is what C writes against
entry_conditions: F's verb contract is settled and not still moving

wave_forecast.outcome: E (#423): re-cut the survivors and run the terminal shipped-vs-obligation check
wave_forecast.why_likely: E is terminal by its own body and runs on what survives
entry_conditions: every other issue in the epic has landed

uncertainty_register.unknown: Does an in-session Task-tool subagent share its parent's already-launched MCP server?
uncertainty_register.affects: Whether per-dispatch config generation is necessary at all, and DC3's verdict
uncertainty_register.settle_by: Running g3 (the separation/inheritance gate) before g1-integrate
uncertainty_register.current_evidence: External-process dispatch is served by ${VAR} expansion in a shared committed config — reviewer-verified, two dispatches, two identities. The in-session case is untested.
uncertainty_register.next_probe: g3, whose handoff is already written

parked_possibilities: Description trimming and the bare-descriptions control arm
A third door beyond CLI and MCP
Concurrency beyond the two-instance separation test

wave_evidence.claim: F's door is up and serving through typed tools
wave_evidence.expected: A cold agent drives a spine to DONE through the tools alone with no malformed calls
wave_evidence.observed: A throwaway spine driven to DONE through the 7 tools; NOT a cold agent on a real role spine

wave_evidence.claim: Same-gate equivalence holds as a property over every gate carrying an imperative
wave_evidence.observed: Byte-identity proven for one SAMPLED gate, with a mutate-to-red-and-revert control; the population check is g2 and was not reached

wave_evidence.claim: Spine-management cost falls, attributably to the door
wave_evidence.expected: Counts per arm, both sides of the door, CLI baseline re-measured
wave_evidence.observed: NOT MEASURED — g4 not reached. No counts exist.

wave_evidence.claim: Inheritance fails closed for a subagent with no special configuration
wave_evidence.expected: Refusal or no identity, never the parent's lease, proven against a positive control
wave_evidence.observed: NOT MEASURED — g3 not reached. Separately, the Admiral measured two spines in this run sharing one session id, so the defect is live in the tree.

wave_evidence.claim: Project-scope .mcp.json cannot serve a cold agent, so per-dispatch generation is required
wave_evidence.observed: FALSIFIED TWICE. Live sessions do not hot-reload .mcp.json (holds). But 'cannot serve a cold agent' omitted --allowedTools and measured the per-tool permission gate; and the replacement claim 'a shared file cannot key identity per agent' is false — ${VAR} expansion does exactly that, verified by two dispatches from one directory against one committed config returning two different spines.
wave_evidence.source: g1 cold reviewer BLOCK, reproduced by commander-424

wave_evidence.claim: The suite is green on the F branch
wave_evidence.observed: 2163 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed after merging origin/main; PR #533 OPEN, MERGEABLE

discrepancies.signal: g1-integrate is blocked by its own cold reviewer, and the block cannot be resolved without a fact the plan scheduled two gates later.
discrepancies.evidence: Reviewer BLOCK on gen_mcp_config.py's justification (not its code — protected-intent items verified, engine diff empty). Necessity turns on whether an in-session Task-tool subagent shares its parent's MCP server. That fact IS DC3, planned at g3.
discrepancies.reason: Repair is evidence-led: the blocking evidence is obtainable, and its gate already has a written handoff.

discrepancies.signal: The plan placed a claim at g1 and its evidence at g3.
discrepancies.evidence: commander-424 names this as its own defect and recommends running g3 first; g2 and g3 handoffs are already written and its leases are released for a clean claim.
discrepancies.reason: Gate order must put evidence before the claim that depends on it.

discrepancies.signal: map_orient.py reports DEGRADED-NO-MAP on a repo with a live enforced map at map/INDEX.md, because it never probes map/.
discrepancies.evidence: commander-424 planned map-first while map-blind and then built ceremony around a confident wrong negative.
discrepancies.reason: Real defect, outside F's scope; it belongs on the board rather than in this wave.

discrepancies.signal: The engine heartbeat is not a liveness signal for a role that blocks on a foreground child; it read 70 minutes stale while the Commander produced a probe, a plan, a crew review and a replan packet.
discrepancies.evidence: Admiral measurement, 2026-08-09, corroborated across five rail firings.
discrepancies.reason: An observation for the retrospective. A rule for future agents belongs in docs/agents/* and is the human's call.

discrepancies.signal: DC5's first numerator counted server-side, where a client-side schema rejection never arrives.
discrepancies.evidence: The cold critic showed the measure could not lose: counting from the server log structurally hides exactly the fumbles the door gets credit for avoiding. Corrected to invocation attempts from the driving agent's record, identical across arms, order-controlled.
discrepancies.reason: Falsified and already replaced by a sound design; the corrected design is the run's most reusable output.

repo_state.map_status: map/INDEX.md is live and enforced by a freshness test; map_orient.py does not probe it and reports DEGRADED-NO-MAP (D2)
